# multisiteDGP <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/joonho112/multisiteDGP/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/joonho112/multisiteDGP/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
<!-- badges: end -->

multisiteDGP simulates the summary data of a multisite trial: one estimated
effect and one standard error per site. You choose the number of sites, the
distribution of the site effects, and the precision of the site estimates.
The package returns a data frame that holds the true site effects next to
their estimates. Such data are used to study estimators of site effects and
of their distribution, and to plan trials and meta-analyses. The model
follows Lee et al. (2025).

## Installation

Install the package from GitHub with the remotes package.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("joonho112/multisiteDGP")
```

## Example

A design holds the settings of a simulation, and a preset is a function that
returns a complete design. `sim_multisite()` simulates one data set from a
design.

```{r simulate}
library(multisiteDGP)

dat <- sim_multisite(preset_education_modest(), seed = 1)
dat
```

Each row is a site. `tau_j` is the true site effect, `tau_j_hat` is its
estimate, and `se_j` is the standard error of the estimate. `summary()`
prints diagnostics of the simulated data.

```{r summary}
summary(dat)
```

A status compares a row with its target or with a fixed rule. The rules of
the first three blocks allow for the sampling error of 50 sites. The standard
deviation of these 50 site effects (0.166) is within two standard errors of
the design value (0.2), so the `sigma_tau` row passes. The `warn` on the
average margin of error describes the design, in which single sites are
estimated with little precision. `plot_effects()` draws the estimates with
their 95 percent intervals and the true site effects.

```{r effects, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "Estimates with 95 percent intervals and true site effects for 50 sites, ordered by estimate."}
plot_effects(dat)
```

## What is in the package

- Six distributions for the site effects (normal, Student t, skew-normal,
  asymmetric Laplace, a two-component mixture, a point mass with a slab) and
  user-supplied distributions.
- Standard errors derived from simulated site sizes with `sim_multisite()`,
  or set directly from a target informativeness with `sim_meta()`.
- Dependence between the site effects and their precision, set through a
  rank correlation.
- Site-level covariates in the site effects.
- Diagnostics of each simulated data set, and `scenario_audit()` for a grid
  of designs built with `design_grid()`.
- Nine presets, plots of the simulated data, and converters to the column
  names that metafor and baggr expect.

## Learn more

- [Get started with multisiteDGP](https://joonho112.github.io/multisiteDGP/articles/multisiteDGP.html)
  runs one simulation and explains the output.
- [The data-generating model](https://joonho112.github.io/multisiteDGP/articles/model.html)
  states the model and maps its symbols to the arguments.
- [Diagnostics and presets](https://joonho112.github.io/multisiteDGP/articles/diagnostics-and-presets.html)
  explains the diagnostics, their thresholds, and the nine presets.

## Citation

`citation("multisiteDGP")` gives the reference for the package. The model is
described in this paper.

Lee, J., Che, J., Rabe-Hesketh, S., Feller, A., & Miratrix, L. (2025).
Improving the estimation of site-specific effects and their distribution in
multisite trials. *Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics*, 50(5),
731-764. <https://doi.org/10.3102/10769986241254286>
